cubecl.delivery: The source `ServerLogger` sends compilation messages through an async channel; the file sink writes one complete record and flushes on each logger write. This harness waits for five identical file-size/event-count observations 25ms apart after each response; this is a quiet-period barrier, not a synchronous CubeCL acknowledgement.
cubecl.logging_level: Full (CUBECL_DEBUG_LOG path selects CompilationLogLevel::Full and source formatting)
cubecl.record_cost: CubeCL emits records from the compilation/load path only; `CompiledKernel` Full formatting and any C++ source formatting occur only on new compilation. The debug env also enables medium profiling output, so timings are explicitly instrumented.

pynndescent.method: live Numba CPUDispatcher identity and public signatures/count snapshots before and after every constructor call, performed outside the constructor timer
pynndescent.proof_scope: No newly visible Numba dispatcher/signature in the timed call proves the observed dispatcher set was post-warmup; Numba exposes no general public compilation event counter here, so this is explicitly a dispatcher-snapshot signal, not a claim about transient unseen dispatchers.

compile_contamination.strategy: One in-process warmup per implementation. Reject and rerun a CUDA sample if its stabilized per-worker CubeCL log gains compilation markers; reject and rerun PyNNDescent if its live dispatcher count or compiled signatures change. Keep every rejected sample and its evidence in this object.

configuration.ipc: persistent Rust process; stdin/stdout JSONL {op:warmup|build,seed,k,cap}; serial requests
configuration.order: ten trials; baseline/candidate/PyNNDescent rotated one-at-a-time; no overlap
configuration.timer: CUDA host input through upload, construction, sync and materialized host IDs/distances; PyNNDescent constructor including trees plus neighbor_graph read; disk IO excluded
